name: js-only-activation
method: Looked for the pattern: a CSS rule sets `display: none` on a base selector, and only adds `display: block|flex|grid` when paired with `.is-active` / `.active` / `.is-open` / `[data-active]` modifier. If the modifier is added by JS only and there is no PHP-side fallback adding it (`class="foo is-active"` in render.php / template), the UI is broken when JS fails to load.

result.css_pattern: display:none on base; display:flex when .is-open or .is-active
result.where_class_added: src/blocks/shared-ui/view.js (multiple toggle sites, e.g. line 463, 470 around the editModalMediaId state)
result.php_fallback: Intentional — modals are interaction-driven; no SSR fallback expected. JS-required by design.
result.verdict: Acceptable. Modals only open from clicks; no SSR state to mirror.

result.css_pattern: transform: translateY(100%); opacity:0 on base; .show variant slides in

result.php_fallback: Yes — render.php emits the first tab with `is-active` class baked in. So the page renders the first tab without JS; only secondary tab switching needs JS.
result.verdict: OK — graceful degradation: first tab visible without JS.

result.css_pattern: display:none on base; .is-active when results present (1.2.0 search autocomplete)
result.php_fallback: None — server-rendered combobox listbox is empty at first render. Acceptable since the suggestions only have meaning after the user types.

notes: Zero real findings. Every JS-only display-toggle pattern is either (a) interaction-only (modals, toasts) where SSR doesn't apply, or (b) has an SSR-baked first-tab/first-state fallback. The 1.2.0 additions (Edit modal, search autocomplete suggestions, Bulk action toolbar) all follow the same disciplined pattern. Bulk action toolbar is server-rendered with all controls present from the start (admin only, JS enriches but does not gate). No regressions.
